titulo: The one-page report in the owner's language + 30-day plan
lead: Nobody reads a long report. The owner wants to know what you found, what you recommend, what's left out, and what happens each week. All on one page, in their own words, no acronyms. This lesson pulls together what you did in the course and builds your plan with dates.
objetivo: write the one-page report in the owner's language, with 3 findings, 1 recommendation, what's left out, and weekly milestones.

aprende.t: Swap jargon for the owner's language
The 4-week plan with a visible milestone
Pull the whole course into a plan with dates

hero_alt: The owner of a small clinic reads a single printed sheet while the consultant points to a passage.

secoes.sub: The four deliverables that become the report. Click an exercise to see the "done when".

degraus.saida: Script, word-for-word phrases, and an agreed count.
degraus.passo: The foundation of everything: without a recent case and a counted number, the rest of the diagnosis becomes opinion.

degraus.saida: Where to look first, with a reason.
degraus.passo: Requires the interview. The scores come from what the owner said, and they check them at the debrief.

degraus.saida: File of tested rules, with an owner and a date.
degraus.passo: Requires the matrix. Three cases, the pattern, and the rules tested on new cases (lessons 4 and 5).

degraus.saida: One recommended, the cuts, and the risk checklist.
degraus.passo: Requires the rules. Score, cut with a reason, and check data and channel (lessons 6 and 7) before writing the page.

resultado.titulo: At the end of the diagnosis
resultado.texto: A page the owner understands, with one safe recommendation and a 30-day plan.

rolagem_fim.texto: Interview, matrix, rules, and recommendation. Each deliverable uses the previous one; the report only puts together what already exists.

secoes.legenda: Mandatory order: each deliverable uses what the previous one produced.

secoes.sub: Four rules that apply to the whole page.

texto: Swap the technical noun for what changes on their Monday.
"Assistant with a knowledge base" becomes "answers just like the front desk, using your insurance table".
Quote the owner at least twice, using the exact sentence you noted in the interview.
They read it and recognize their own problem, said the way they say it.
Say what AI doesn't do: it doesn't decide for them, it doesn't get everything right at the start, it doesn't know what isn't written down, it doesn't update itself.
That's why the plan starts with human approval. Said up front, this reassures; discovered later, it becomes a complaint.
Read it out loud to someone who isn't in the field. If the person asks "what is that?", rewrite it.
Would you say that sentence at the counter of the bakery? If not, it's jargon.

secoes.sub: The report fits on one page. Scope without price: price is a conversation for Selling with AI. Replace what's between < > with your own.

blocos.conteudo:
# Diagnosis — <business> — <date>
Prepared by <consultant> for <owner>

## 1. What I heard (3 to 5 sentences)
<situation in the owner's words, with 1 literal sentence in quotes>

## 2. Three findings
1. <finding> — <evidence: case, count, matrix score>
2. <finding> — <evidence>
3. <finding> — <evidence>

## 3. The recommendation (just one)
<what to do, in which area, with what observable result in 30 days>
Automation level at the start: <1 / 2 / 3>   Who approves: <person>

## 4. What is left out, and why
- <candidate>: <doesn't need AI / not now> — <reason>

## 5. 30-day plan
Week 1: <visible milestone>
Week 2: <visible milestone>
Week 3: <visible milestone>
Week 4: <visible milestone>

## 6. Scope
Includes: <...>
Does not include: <...>
Risks and rules checked on <date>: <personal data, channel>

"Knowledge-base assistant"            → "answers just like the front desk, using your price list"
"Qualification flow with handoff"     → "sorts out who wants to book and calls you when it's an exception"
"Event-triggered automation"          → "the message goes out on its own when the appointment is booked"
"Examples for the model to learn from" → "learns from your cases and repeats your way of doing it"
"Phased human approval"               → "at first, nothing goes out without you or the front desk approving it"

[ ] Fits on one page
[ ] No technical acronym without an explanation
[ ] At least 2 literal sentences from the owner, in quotes
[ ] Each finding has evidence (case, count, or score)
[ ] One recommendation, not several
[ ] What is left out is written down, with a reason
[ ] Each week has a milestone the owner can see
[ ] The limit of AI is stated
[ ] No number without a source; no client personal data
[ ] Passed the grandparent test

Clínica Vila Serena (fictional) — after-hours questions on WhatsApp
Week 1: count for the week done (baseline) and rules file approved by the owner
Week 2: assistant set up in testing, checked against 15 written cases (how to do it: course 2)
Week 3: live at level 1: the front desk approves each reply prepared at night, every morning
Week 4: front desk and owner trained (course 2); comparison with week 1's count; decision to continue, adjust, or shut it off

  • All 4 weeks have a visible milestone, and week 4 has a decision: continue, adjust, or shut it off.

• A 12-page report with a table of everything.
  • Three competing recommendations.
  • A savings number with no source ("it will save 10 hours").
  • A dollar amount in the diagnosis: price and proposal follow Selling with AI.

secoes.sub: Four questions about the whole diagnosis.

perguntas.p: How many recommendations does the one-page report include?
opcoes: One, with what is left out explained.
All the ones the matrix scored.
Three, so the owner can pick the one they prefer.
perguntas.explica: One clear recommendation. Several competing ones look like a shopping list; cuts with a reason show judgment.

perguntas.p: What is the order of the diagnosis deliverables?
perguntas.explica: Each deliverable builds on the one before: without an interview there is no grade with criteria; without written rules there is no safe recommendation.

perguntas.p: "Assistant with a knowledge base" in the owner's language becomes:
opcoes: "Generative artificial intelligence system with its own database."
"Answers just like the front desk, using your price list."
perguntas.explica: A result with a routine verb, not technology. Passes the grandparent test.

perguntas.p: What does week 4 of the 30-day plan need to have?
opcoes: The signing of the maintenance contract.
The launch of every project on the map.
A complete 12-page report with tables for all five areas of the business.
A comparison with the baseline and the decision to continue, adjust, or shut it down.
perguntas.explica: The pilot ends by measuring against the week 1 count and deciding with the owner. What comes after is course 2.

itens.texto: Interview with consent, a recent case, and silence; a missing number becomes a count.
Matrix of the 5 areas, tested IF/THEN rules, and 6 axes with what not to recommend.
In the owner's language, with risk checked, one recommendation, and four weeks with a milestone.
